chapter: San Francisco, the So Different Orchestra and Johnny
title: Baron Long's Tavern in Watts, Valentino and the movie-star clientele
summary: In Watts the band plays for Rudolph Valentino's dancing act, Harry Richman and Cliff Friend, with Hollywood stars in the audience.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And it was in the basement there, and that's where we played for two years. Then we came here and played for Baron Long out at Watts at Baron Long's Tavern, where Rudolph Valentino was the dancing...I mean, he had a dancing act, and the other boy was a singer. What did I tell you his name was?

Harry Richman. Cliff Friend, who wrote "Just A Baby's Prayer At Twilight" was a singer there, and they used to have all of the clientele, 'course, was all of the movie stars-- Blanche Sweet, Charlie Chaplin, Fatty Arbuckle and all of the oldtimers, you know, was there every night 'cause they'd never heard a band like ours.
I think you mentioned Mary Pickford, didn't you?
Mary Pickford, Jack Pickford and Lottie Pickford --they all used to come there.
